Job Description:
About Chainlink Labs

Chainlink Labs is one of the primary contributing developers of Chainlink, the standard for onchain finance enabling high-quality data, secure cross-chain interoperability, and compliant connectivity across global markets. Chainlink powers leading tokenized assets, financial institutions, market infrastructures, and decentralized applications by providing secure access to real-world data, cross-chain messaging, and blockchain connectivity across any network. The Chainlink standard has enabled tens of trillions of dollars in transaction value and is helping unify global markets onchain. Many of the world’s largest financial services institutions have also adopted Chainlink’s standards and infrastructure, including Swift, Euroclear, Mastercard, Fidelity International, UBS, S&P Dow Jones Indices, FTSE Russell, WisdomTree, ANZ, Aave, Polymarket, Lido, and many others.
Chainlink Labs is a world-class team of developers, researchers, and capital markets experts, and has ranked among Fortune's Best Workplaces in Technology, Fortune's Best Medium Workplace, and the Top 100 Global Most Loved Workplaces. Learn more at or.
About The Role
Join Chainlink Labs, a leading decentralized oracle network company, as a high-impact Executive Assistant and strategic thought partner to our senior leadership. In this dynamic role, you’ll go beyond traditional support—serving as the right hand to our executives and playing a key role in driving operational excellence. From managing complex calendars and high-stakes meetings to navigating sensitive information with discretion, you’ll be trusted to anticipate needs, streamline workflows, and help power our fast-paced, high-performance journey. If you’re proactive, sharp, and thrive in an environment where every day is different, we want to meet you. We don't have an assigned team for this role and will put people where they will best shine! 
For this role, we are ideally looking for someone based in the NYC area. This role will be remote with occasional travel to our office when required. We are also open to other EST remote locations
Your Impact

- Act as a gatekeeper for the executive’s time and focus - managing and prioritizing requests from across the business and the external ecosystem.

- Successfully coordinate and execute department meetings and communications, ensuring smooth collaboration and efficient information flow.

- Demonstrate the highest level of discretion when handling sensitive information, recognizing the importance of safeguarding the interests of Chainlink Labs.

- Exhibit excellent written communication skills, as you will be communicating largely in text and taking important notes for various engagements.

- Be a right-hand person to the executive team, partnering with them to help efficiently navigate their private and professional lives.

- Own and deliver on a wide variety of projects and initiatives for the executive team.

Requirements

- Experience delivering a high touch support model, anticipating needs, and establishing seamless processes across core executive support tasks, e.g. scheduling, travel, communications, records, and reports.

- Experience as an Executive Assistant managing sensitive data and commitment to maintaining confidentiality within a security-focused company environment.

- Experience in a multi-time-zone/global setting

- Willingness to work outside usual business hours with a high sense of urgency.

- Strong self-management, time management, and organizational skills to effectively handle multiple tasks.

- Excellent written communication level, capable of articulating ideas and communicating clearly in writing.

- Experience using tact, sound business judgment, a solid understanding of our business, and impeccable time management, managing and prioritizing the C-Suite’s schedule and business obligations.

Preferred Requirements

- Experience in small-medium tech startup environments, accustomed to working in agile and ownership-driven settings.

- Event planning experience, demonstrating the ability to organize successful team offsites for the executive’s department.

- Experience working on a team of highly collaborative EA’s, sharing insights, representing the executives effectively, and contributing positively to our company culture.

Remote Academic Coach & Student Assistant (Part-Time, ~10 hours/week)
The steady partner who helps a high-achieving student master hard material and never miss a deadline.
About the Role
Seamless Assist is hiring a part-time Academic Coach & Student Assistant for a US-based family. You will work one-on-one, online, with their daughter, a motivated high-school student taking classes a year ahead of her grade, including several college-level Advanced Placement (AP) courses. This role reports to the student's parent.
Why This Role Exists
The student doesn't need to be taught from scratch. She is carrying a demanding, writing-heavy course load, and the pressure is in the volume: essays, problem sets, labs, tests and extracurricular deadlines all landing in the same week. This role exists to give her a sharp, organised partner who can keep up with advanced material, help her work through the hardest parts, and keep her schedule under control so nothing slips.
Her Current Classes

- AP Microeconomics & Macroeconomics

- AP Biology

- AP English Language & Composition

- AP US History

- Pre-Calculus

- Spanish 4

- Journalism & News Production

You don't need to be an expert in every subject. You do need to be strong in several of them, especially writing-heavy courses (AP English Language, AP US History) and at least one of economics, biology or maths.
What You'll Actually Be Doing
Academic coaching (about 70% of your time)

- Run live one-on-one video sessions to work through homework, problem sets, essays and test preparation.

- Explain difficult concepts clearly and check that she can explain them back.

- Review essays and written work for argument, structure, evidence and citations, including AP-style timed essays.

- Build practice questions, review plans and study guides ahead of tests and the AP exams in May.

- Learn how each course is taught and graded (syllabi, teacher rubrics, the College Board AP course frameworks) and coach to them.

- Coach, never complete. Her work must always be her own, in line with her school's academic integrity rules.

Planning and student assistant support (about 30% of your time)

- Run a weekly planning session: map every class's assignments, tests and deadlines into a shared calendar and task list.

- Keep her schedule current across classes, activities and appointments, with study time blocked in.

- Send short reminders before deadlines and confirm work was actually submitted.

- Track grades and flag early when something starts to slip.

- Send the parent a short weekly progress update.

Schedule
About 10 hours per week. Sessions fall on weekday afternoons and evenings, US Pacific Time (roughly 3:30–8:30 pm PT), plus one short weekend planning session. You must be reliably available in that window.
Who Will Succeed in This Role
This is a high-trust role with a bright, busy teenager. You will need real subject depth, patience, and the organisational discipline of a strong executive assistant.

- You explain things clearly and can tell the difference between "I get it" and actually getting it.

- You are a strong writer and can give specific, useful feedback on an argumentative essay.

- You run your own life from a calendar and a task list, and you follow up without being asked.

- You are warm, steady and encouraging, and you hold a high standard.

Requirements

- Bachelor's degree or higher, ideally in education, English, history, economics, biology, mathematics or a related field.

- At least 2 years of tutoring or teaching high-school or first-year university students.

- Strong command of the material in several of the subjects listed above.

- Excellent written and spoken English. Your writing will be assessed during screening.

- Uses AI tools in your daily work (for example Claude, ChatGPT or Gemini) to build study materials and plan faster, and can teach a student to use them responsibly and within school rules.

- Able to work US Pacific Time afternoons and evenings, about 10 hours per week.

- Reliable high-speed internet, a quiet workspace, a webcam and a backup power or internet plan.

- Willing to complete a national police clearance or background check and provide two professional references before starting.

Nice to have

- Experience with the US Advanced Placement (AP) programme, or strong AP, SAT, IB or A-Level results of your own.

- Conversational or better Spanish.

- Journalism, editing or newsroom experience.

- Comfortable in Google Workspace (Calendar, Docs, Drive) and a task tool such as Notion or Todoist.

How We Work
Because this role involves working one-on-one with a teenager, clear safeguards apply. All sessions run on a family-owned video account and are recorded. All messages go through a group channel that includes a parent. There is no private messaging or social-media contact with the student. A background check and references are required before the first paid session.
Pay
Competitive hourly pay, paid monthly in USD. Pay varies by country.
How to Apply
Apply with your CV. Shortlisted candidates will be invited to a short AI-led video interview, a written subject task, an interview with the family and a paid trial session.

- Review proposal history and the Proposal Summary Tracker to identify past clients, architectural firms, and other contacts who previously requested proposals or engaged with the firm but have since become inactive.

- Understand the history of each relationship before initiating contact. Use previous proposals, communication records, and relationship notes to establish context.

- Make outbound phone calls to reconnect with past clients, architects, developers, designers, contractors, and other relevant professional contacts.

- Research new architectural firms, developers, contractors, consultants, and architect-adjacent organizations to expand the firm's target contact list.

- Review target companies' websites, LinkedIn profiles, leadership teams, and recent projects before initiating outreach.

- Develop and maintain a structured outreach cadence, generally following up monthly unless the contact's circumstances or timing call for earlier action.

- Follow up through phone, email, and LinkedIn without relying on a single communication channel.

- Gather feedback from previous prospects when possible, including why proposals were not awarded, pricing concerns, service gaps, or dissatisfaction with existing providers.

- Maintain an organized business development pipeline with accurate relationship statuses, outreach stages, opportunity notes, next actions, and follow-up dates.

- Recognize stalled conversations, overdue follow-ups, and opportunities that require renewed attention.

- Support re-engagement campaigns and outreach strategies intended to generate meetings, referrals, and future business opportunities.

2. Meeting Coordination & Relationship Management

- Schedule business development calls, meetings, and in-person lunches between leadership and high-priority contacts.

- Coordinate calendars and ensure promising conversations translate into defined next steps.

- Draft and send professional outreach emails that reflect the firm's voice, positioning, and previous relationship with the recipient.

- Monitor relevant inbound communications and organize or route client inquiries, drawings, and project requests.

- Keep leadership informed of meaningful responses, potential opportunities, objections, and relationship developments.

- Ensure that important conversations and commitments are followed through rather than left undocumented.

3. Marketing Support & Materials Maintenance

- Maintain organized marketing materials and project reference documents used for business development and relationship-building.

- Help manage the firm's LinkedIn presence by reviewing connection requests, monitoring messages, and identifying relevant industry contacts.

- Research target firms, industry opportunities, and potential partnerships that could expand the business development pipeline.

- Coordinate updates to company materials, including project lists, award announcements, and website content, when applicable.

- Support light social media and online presence updates as directed.

- Organize proposal files, project documents, and communication records so leadership can retrieve the correct information when needed.

- Track proposal and client-request deadlines, missing documents, pending actions, and required follow-ups.

- Maintain documentation and process trackers for outreach, marketing activities, and internal priorities.

- 
Research & Prospecting: Ability to identify relevant target companies, decision-makers, and business opportunities through online research and professional networking platforms.

- 
Independent Execution: Ability to prioritize activities, recognize overdue follow-ups, manage competing responsibilities, and take ownership of results without daily step-by-step supervision.

- 
Organization & Documentation: Consistent and accurate documentation of interactions, relationship context, opportunities, and pending actions.

- 
Microsoft Office Proficiency: Working proficiency in Microsoft Outlook, Word, and Excel.

Proposal Summary / Proposal History Tracker: Reviewing previous proposals and understanding existing relationships.

The Mindset We’re Looking For
The best Executive Support Specialists we’ve worked with share a few traits:

- They’re the person their friends call when they need to figure something out. Not because they always have the answer — but because they know how to think through a problem, ask the right questions, and get to a solution 

- They don’t wait to be told. If they see something that needs to happen, they handle it — then let the client know it’s done, not ask if they should do it

- They treat confidentiality as non-negotiable. What happens in the client’s world stays there — no exceptions, no grey areas 

- They use AI the way a sharp operator would — not as a novelty, but as a tool that makes their output faster and better than anyone who isn’t using it

Who Thrives Here
People who are quietly excellent — not flashy, but consistently sharp, reliable, and ahead of the curve. You don’t need recognition for every task you handle. You find satisfaction in the fact that things run smoothly because of you, even if no one notices the work behind it.

- You treat “that’s not my job” as a reasonable response 

- You let things slip and wait for someone else to notice 

- You’d stay quiet about a mistake to avoid a difficult conversation 

- Confidentiality feels like a guideline rather than a hard rule 

- You’re uncomfortable with shifting priorities and changing plans

- Familiarity with project management tools (ClickUp, Asana, Trello, or Monday.com)

About the role
 The Data Analyst Assistant role is central to our current engagement with a Dubai-based investment firm that requires precise data handling and clear visualization. This position provides the quantitative groundwork that allows our principals to form a view on complex corporate governance and strategy questions. We need an assistant who can organize messy data sets into logical structures that reveal the health and performance of a holding company.
 
About Arabian Private Holdings
 Arabian Private Holdings was founded on the principle that many critical business problems do not fit the traditional large-firm consulting model. A board facing a succession question or a family group weighing a capital injection does not need a team of twelve associates and a hundred-page methodology deck. They need experienced partners who can sit with a problem, form a rigorous view, and defend it. We take on a limited number of mandates to ensure that every client receives direct attention from the principals who are actually accountable for the outcome. Our work covers corporate strategy, governance, and operating model efficiency for some of the most significant family groups, listed corporations, and government entities in the region. We focus on clarity over complexity. We operate as a remote firm, choosing to prioritize the quality of our analysis and the strength of our relationships over traditional office overhead or aggressive growth targets.
 
What you will do 
- Collect and organize financial and operational data from various portfolio companies for a Dubai-based investment.
 
- Clean and validate data sets to ensure accuracy before they are used in client presentations.
 
- Build simple, effective spreadsheets that track performance indicators for large holding companies.
 
- Assist in drafting reports that translate numbers into clear written arguments for our principals.
 
- Monitor industry trends and perform basic market research to support ongoing strategic mandates.
 
- Maintain internal records to ensure that historical client data is easily accessible and correctly categorized.
 
- Prepare charts and graphs that simplify complex financial structures for board-level reviews.
 
- Support the audit of corporate governance documents by cross-referencing quantitative findings with qualitative reports.

What we are looking for 
- A clear understanding of basic statistics and a logical approach to problem-solving.
 
- Proficiency in spreadsheet software with an ability to manage large amounts of information without errors.
 
- Strong written skills and the ability to explain what a set of numbers means in plain English.
 
- Curiosity about how large corporations and family groups operate in different sectors.
 
- Precision in your work, where you check your own calculations before submitting them for review.
 
- A degree or ongoing studies in a quantitative field such as economics, finance, or mathematics.

How we work
 We operate as a fully remote firm, which means we rely on clear documentation and asynchronous communication. Because our work involves sensitive mandates for high-profile clients, we maintain a high standard of professional conduct and data security. You will work closely with a principal who provides direct mentorship and expects you to form your own view on the data you analyze. We do not value long hours for the sake of appearances. Instead, we focus on the rigor of the output and the clarity of the logic. This remote model allows us to hire individuals based on their intellectual capability rather than their physical location, ensuring we can provide the best possible advice to our clients.
 
What the role offers 
- A paid entry-level position with a competitive compensation package for the current market.
 
- Direct exposure to high-level corporate strategy and governance mandates.
 
- Mentorship from experienced principals who have managed some of the largest holding companies in the region.
 
- The flexibility of a permanent, full-time role that is entirely remote.
 
- Practical experience in forming a rigorous view on business performance and portfolio health.

About Blue Oak Consulting
 Blue Oak Consulting provides independent advisory on pricing, portfolio economics, capital allocation, and acquisition assumptions. We are not a traditional consulting firm focused on broad transformation programs or high level strategy decks. Instead, we interrogate specific commercial decisions where the financial stakes are high and the existing narrative is not sufficient. Our team looks past corporate language and P&L complexity to identify where value is leaking or capital is trapped. We work across sectors like software, manufacturing, and healthcare to test whether the assumptions behind a growth plan or an acquisition actually hold under pressure. We are a small, principal led firm where the people who do the work are the ones accountable for the results. We do not take transaction contingent fees, which allows us to be completely honest about whether the economics of a decision make sense. Our goal is to provide clarity through financial discipline and a healthy amount of skepticism.
 
The Role
 This is a full time, permanent position that is conducted entirely in a remote environment. You will work closely with our principals to dig into the numbers provided by our partners, often starting with the Italian infrastructure project. The goal is to move past P&L complexity and find where value might be leaking. You will be expected to think critically and ask why certain numbers exist high up in a spreadsheet, rather than just accepting them as facts. This role offers an attractive and competitive compensation package for an entry level professional looking to gain deep experience in financial analysis.
 
What You Will Be Doing 
- Cleaning and organizing large datasets from various sources to build a clear financial picture.
 
- Testing the logic behind pricing assumptions to see if they survive real world friction.
 
- Helping build financial models that track capital allocation across different infrastructure assets.
 
- Identifying outliers and anomalies in expenditure reports that do not align with the stated narrative.
 
- Updating portfolio economics trackers to reflect new acquisition data.
 
- Collaborating with the team through virtual channels to clarify findings and refine analysis.
 
- Preparing clear summaries of data trends that highlight potential financial risks.
 
- Verifying the accuracy of inputs used in growth forecasts for specific business units.
 
- Assisting in the interrogation of acquisition assumptions for new investment opportunities.

What You Bring 
- A degree or background in finance, economics, mathematics, or a related field with a heavy emphasis on data.
 
- Strong proficiency in Microsoft Excel, including the ability to manage complex formulas and large tables.
 
- A skeptical mindset that enjoys finding inconsistencies in spreadsheets and reports.
 
- Comfort working in a fully remote setting where communication is largely written and specific.
 
- Ability to organize messy data into structured formats without losing important context.
 
- Interest in how large businesses actually spend money and allocate internal capital.
 
- Reliability and a willingness to learn how to scrutinize financial statements at a deep level.
 
- Strong attention to detail, especially when reviewing line items that seem out of place.

What We Offer 
- A fully remote work schedule that provides flexibility and removes the need for a daily commute.
 
- Direct access to firm principals who provide mentorship and clear feedback on your work.
 
- The opportunity to work on high stakes projects, such as our current work with the Italian infrastructure group.
 
- A professional environment focused on logic and evidence rather than corporate politics.
 
- Practical training in financial modeling and capital allocation analysis.
 
- A permanent, stable role within a firm that values individual accountability and results.

 At Blue Oak Consulting, we believe that clarity comes from discipline and a healthy amount of skepticism. We stay through the execution phase of our projects because we know that decisions looking sound in theory often face challenges once they meet reality. This role is a starting point for someone who wants to understand the mechanics of how value is created and protected in large organizations. We value the work over the performance, and we look for assistants who are eager to show how the numbers actually add up without relying on corporate jargon.

Valiantys is a global professional services firm dedicated to helping engineering and service organizations transform how they work, using AI-enabled software delivery, modern ITSM, and platform engineering.

The opportunity
We're hiring a Chief of Staff to support the CEO. This role exists to increase the CEO's leverage, strengthen executive alignment, and improve the quality and pace of key decisions. It is not a substitute for operating leadership and does not own day-to-day company operations. Instead, the Chief of Staff acts as an extension of the CEO to drive clarity, follow-through, and executive coherence across the leadership team.

Location: This role can be located in the United States, (EST, New York City preferred). We offer flexible remote working policy.

What You'll Own
Operating cadence
Design and run the executive operating rhythm across a distributed leadership team. This includes C-suite meeting design, leadership team offsites, and the CEO's 1:1 cadence - ensuring each forum has a clear purpose, the right participants, the right pre-work, and concrete outputs.

Decision governance
Build and maintain the decision-making infrastructure for the exec team: RACI frameworks, decision logs, real-time commitment tracking. Make the implicit explicit. Document decisions as they're made, track what was decided, by whom, and what happens next.

Strategic progress tracking
Create the scorecards, dashboards, and executive reporting rhythms that give the CEO clear visibility into transformation priorities, business risks, and decisions requiring intervention. Partner closely with the COO and executive team to synthesize progress, surface slippage early, and sharpen the quality of discussion at the top. This role owns executive-level transparency and escalation.

Executive forum quality
Own the output quality of the company's most important executive forums. This means ensuring the right pre-reads exist, decisions are captured in real time, follow-through is tracked, and unresolved issues are escalated quickly. The standard is that every significant forum produces clarity, accountability, and momentum.

Executive communications
Craft the materials that shape the company's most important conversations: board updates, executive memos, decision briefs, CEO communications, investor-ready narratives, and sensitive internal messaging. Turn complex issues into crisp, well-structured communication tailored to senior audiences. Ensure the CEO enters key discussions with sharp materials, clear points of view, and decision-ready framing.

Thought partnership
Serve as a trusted sounding board to the CEO on strategic priorities, sensitive issues, and cross-functional tradeoffs. Translate complex discussions into structured options, clear decisions, and actionable next steps. - A proven operator who has built executive operating rhythm in a 300 to 600 person professional services or B2B services business and knows what well-run looks like

- Fluency in driving accountability through influence: building trust with senior leaders, holding peers accountable as a partner, and earning a mandate rather than asserting one

- The ability to hold the full operating plan, see dependencies, and anticipate second-order effects before they surface as problems

- Structured thinking that turns complexity and conflicting inputs into clear options and decisions

- Sound judgment and discretion with sensitive information and competing priorities, and a clear sense of when to push, escalate, or stay behind the scenes

- 8-12 years of experience, including 2+ years in a Chief of Staff, Executive Strategy & Operations, GM, or equivalent operating role

- MBA or equivalent; strategy consulting background a plus, not a requirement

- A proven record of designing and building operating infrastructure for a distributed executive teams

- Professional services, consulting, or B2B services background strongly preferred, , with a working understanding of the economics and the consultative model

- Meaningful experience in transformation contexts: strategic pivot, M&A integration, or major operational change

- PE-backed or high-growth experience, board exposure, and strong executive writing are each a plus

- The CEO is spending more time on the highest-value strategic priorities and less time on coordination overhead

- The COO has more capacity to scale the business and lead day-to-day operations

- Executive forums produce clearer decisions, better follow-through, and faster escalation of critical issues

About the Role: 

As a Senior Executive Assistant, you will support four to five members of Maven’s C-suite and play an important role in helping them use their time effectively. You’ll manage complex calendars, coordinate travel and meetings, anticipate needs, and keep priorities and follow-ups moving. - Manage complex calendars and scheduling. Coordinate internal and external meetings across competing priorities, maintain clean calendars, and proactively resolve conflicts. Build in appropriate preparation, travel, and follow-up time.

- Support special projects. Take ownership of selected projects that improve executive operations, team coordination, or the EA team’s shared resources. Identify and implement process improvements for your executives and the EA team.

- Own logistics of events and gatherings. Coordinate executive and team meetings, offsites, dinners, celebrations, and other events, managing logistics and working with internal partners and vendors often on the ground.

- Project manage cross-functional strategic initiatives. Be a key player in project management of key projects within your executive’s teams and function, enabling your exec to ensure effective ways of working with their teams and achieving key strategic goals.

- Use AI thoughtfully to improve how the work gets done. Apply approved AI tools to streamline tasks such as meeting preparation, travel briefs, communications, follow-up tracking, and repeatable workflows. - 4-6 years of experience as an Executive Assistant, including experience supporting senior or C-suite executives; experience supporting multiple executives is a plus.

- Strong organization and attention to detail, with the ability to manage several priorities and adapt as plans change.

- Sound judgment and the confidence to ask clarifying questions, make recommendations, and escalate risks or blockers early.

- Comfort working in a fast-paced, high-growth environment, with the ability to shift priorities quickly.

- A proactive and hands-on approach: you anticipate needs, prepare ahead, and follow through without needing repeated reminders.

- Clear, polished communication across email, Slack, meetings, and in-person interactions.

- The discretion and reliability to handle confidential company, personnel, and executive information.

- Responsiveness and reliability. Reachable for urgent matters, with the ability to support executives consistently.

- Experience coordinating complex meetings, travel, and events.

- Comfort using Google Workspace, Slack, project-management tools, and virtual meeting platforms.

- Curiosity about AI and experience using AI tools in your work, or the initiative to learn and apply them responsibly.

- A team player with a collaborative working style, strong accountability, and extreme ownership, who shares knowledge, supports coverage, and helps the EA team work well together.

- Flexibility to adjust your schedule occasionally, including for travel or time-zone differences, to meet business needs or time-sensitive changes.
